subject: Demo recap and POC launch plan — ZenTerra
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@zenterra.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + proposed next steps (POC kickoff)

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. I wanted to capture the key takeaways and propose a concise POC sequence so we can get you to a meaningful evaluation without spending calendar months.

Recap highlights:
- We showed intent extraction, policy-aware redaction, and a live end-to-end inference flow for your ticket triage example.
- You liked the latency profile and the ability to pin a model variant for consistency across the trial.
- Main concern: data connectivity and audit log retention for compliance.

Proposed POC (high level):
1) Sandbox setup (week 0–1): Redwood provides a VPC-connected sandbox and a test service account. ZenTerra provides a 2–3k sample ticket dataset and an S3 read-only role.
2) Evaluation sprint (week 2–3): Run ~10k simulated calls across your typical distribution (short/long tickets). Track latency P95, token cost/unit, and intent accuracy on a 200-item labeled set.
3) Signoff (end week 3): Decision based on success criteria below.

Draft success criteria (please confirm or edit):
- Intent extraction accuracy ≥ 88% on labeled set (precision/recall balanced)
- Avg token cost < $0.004 per request at expected throughput (after Redwood batching)
- P95 latency < 250 ms for the 95th percentile under realistic concurrency (as measured in the sandbox)
- Audit logs available with 90-day retention and exportable CSVs for compliance review

I attached the demo recording and a short POC outline (poc-outline-zenterra.xlsx). If this aligns with your expectations, can we lock a kickoff window the week of Mar 4? If not, please propose alternatives and edit the success criteria inline.

Thanks — happy to jump back on a call to walk through the plan.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

Hi Hannah —

Thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side before we confirm dates:
1) Data access: We can provide a redacted S3 bucket, but can you confirm Redwood's options for in-transit encryption and whether any data will be persisted outside the sandbox?
2) Metrics: For intent accuracy, can you run an initial baseline with our 200 labeled items and share the confusion matrix?
3) Timeline: Mar 4 is tight for our infra team; would Mar 11–15 work instead?
4) Compliance: Our legal team wants confirmation that audit logs are exportable and include request/response hashes for traceability — tagging them here so they can review.

Looping Samir (engineering) and legal.

—Emily

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@zenterra.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Feb 2028 14:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed next steps (POC kickoff)

Hi Emily — thanks for the quick questions — answers below and an adjusted plan if Mar 11 works.

1) Data access & persistence
- Encryption: TLS in transit; we support customer-managed keys (KMS) for at-rest in Dedicated/Private. For the sandbox we'll use AES-256 and can enable a scoped customer key on request.
- Persistence: By default sandbox logs and KV caches are stored for the trial window. We can configure TTLs and a full purge after the POC. We'll document the retention policy and export steps.

2) Baseline run with your labels
- Please upload the 200 labeled items to the Drive folder (link below) or grant the S3 role. We will run a baseline within 48 hours of receiving them and share a confusion matrix + per-intent precision/recall.

3) Timeline (Mar 11 kickoff) — updated 3-week plan
- Week 0 (Mar 11–15): Sandbox & connection, baseline run, ingestion validation (owner: ZenTerra IT for dataset; Redwood infra for sandbox).
- Week 1 (Mar 18–22): Integration + 10k simulated calls, initial metric collection.
- Week 2 (Mar 25–29): Tuning, repeat runs, final metrics + handoff pack.
- Decision meeting: Apr 1 (final signoff).

4) Audit logs
- Export: CSV exports of request metadata (timestamp, request id, model variant, token counts) are available. For response-level export we can provide hashed responses; we will work with legal on exact format.

POC responsibilities (short):
- ZenTerra: provide sample dataset, agree on labeled baseline, grant S3/Drive access, review results.
- Redwood: sandbox, baseline run, instrument metrics, weekly syncs, 2 support seats during active runs.

Next steps
- If Mar 11 works, please confirm by EOD Wed (Feb 28) so we can schedule infra and reserve the sandbox.
- I'll attach an SOW skeleton for internal review — Ben, Marissa: can you review the POC-SOW-draft.docx and advise if any contract gating is needed for a sandbox with temporary data access?

Drive folder (upload labels here): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBz-zen-poc
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/ZenTerra

Regards,
Hannah
